bullets.title: ORCL: Beats Q4 but heavy capex ($70B net FY27) and equity raise sink stock -9% premarket
bullets.body: Oracle reported F4Q26 revenue of $19.18B (+0.4% above consensus) and EPS of $2.11 (vs. $1.96 est), with cloud infra (OCI) growing 92-93% YoY and RPO surging to $638B. However, FY27 guidance of $90B revenue and $8.05 EPS was offset by $90-95B gross ($70B net cash) capex guidance and a planned $40B financing package ($20B equity ATM + $20B debt). Stock fell ~9-10% premarket. Citi (Buy, $330 PT), JPM (OW, $210 PT), UBS (Buy, $285 PT), and D.A. Davidson all maintained bullish stances, citing strong bookings and OCI trajectory, while viewing the stock reaction as overly punitive.

bullets.title: MU: Wolfe raises PT to $1,250; bull thesis on DRAM/NAND/HBM pricing cycle through CY27
bullets.body: Wolfe Research raised its MU CY27 estimates to $226B revenue and $135 EPS (vs. street $186B/$107) on sustained DRAM price increases of 35% q/q in 2Q, 15% in 3Q, and 40% YoY for HBM in CY27. PT raised to $1,250 from $550. MU trades at just 7.2x FY27E EPS vs. the historical 10x through-cycle multiple, with supply constrained through CY28. LTAs with price/volume minimums and penalty clauses set a new precedent for the memory market.

bullets.title: INTC: BofA double-upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $135 from $96 on better CPU outlook
bullets.body: BofA analyst Vivek Arya upgraded Intel to Buy from Underperform and raised the price target to $135 from $96, implying ~26% upside from the ~$107 current price. Stock +5.3% premarket. MSI Chairman credits Intel and AMD for easing the CPU shortage since Q2, with overall server demand described as very strong.

bullets.title: COHR & LITE: JPM reiterates OW; ~20% pullback on CPO concerns deemed overblown
bullets.body: JPM's Samik Chatterjee argues the ~20% pullback in optical names is overdone: NVDA's CPO ramp is tracking on or better than plan, Lumentum reports CPO-supported switch mix now >50% (vs. 40-50% prior), and COHR/LITE now trade at ~25x CY28 consensus earnings for 40%+ EPS growth (sub-1x PEG). Pentagon listing of Chinese suppliers Innolight and Eoptolink could further accelerate U.S. supply chain shift toward COHR and LITE. DoD developments could become a structural tailwind.

bullets.title: WDC & STX: JPM raises PTs to $650/$920; HDD pricing cycle accelerating on AI demand
bullets.body: JPM raises WDC PT to $650 (33% upside) and STX PT to $920 (13% upside) as HDD pricing accelerates, with YoY price growth modeling +11% for WDC and +10% for STX in FY27. Neither company is adding unit capacity, supporting a durable pricing cycle. FY27 gross margins forecast at 58.6% for WDC and 54.5% for STX, with 90%+ EPS growth expected in FY27. Hyperscalers signing LTAs extending to 2032 for supply assurance.

bullets.title: ADBE: Reporting tonight; CEO transition and AI disruption risk cloud print
bullets.body: ADBE reports after the close (consensus EPS $5.82, revenue $6.45B). UBS flags FY26 ARR growth guidance already cut to 10.2% from 11.5%, and unlikely to raise FY27 guidance. Stock is down 33% YTD amid AI disruption concerns; CEO transition is the primary investor focus. Wolfe notes the All-SaaS index is trading at 5.2x FY+2 EV/Sales, with IGV down 13.2% YTD.

bullets.title: SMCI: Wolfe initiates at Peer Perform; governance risks offset AI demand tailwinds
bullets.body: Wolfe Research initiates SMCI at Peer Perform with a $26-31 fair value range (9-11x CY28E EPS of $2.90). SMCI priced a $7B equity raise ($1.25B common + $3.75B convertible preferred + $2B ATM) and co-founder Wally Liaw was indicted, though the NVIDIA relationship remains intact. AI server demand from CoreWeave, xAI, and Tesla supports the growth profile but customer concentration and governance risks cap the multiple.

bullets.title: DKNG: Prediction market volumes surge; Opco and Jefferies both bullish on new vertical
bullets.body: DraftKings prediction market volumes grew 34% m/m to $3.1B annualized in May (consumer +24%, maker +42%). Oppenheimer models $864M revenue/$426M contribution profit in 2027 and >$1.2B revenue in 2028. Jefferies notes no OSB cannibalization, prediction markets access ~50% of US population previously excluded from OSB, and regulatory tailwinds are building (CA/GA closer to legalization). Estimated May PM revenues of ~$11M are immaterial to 2Q guidance but demonstrate execution.

bullets.title: META: Forced to unwind Manus AI acquisition after China regulatory block
bullets.body: China's NDRC blocked Meta's $2B Manus acquisition and ordered assets restored to original state. Since early June, Meta has ceased data-sharing with Manus and internal memos indicate the unit is being 'sunsetted.' Meta and Manus face potential penalties if the deal cannot be fully rescinded. Media & Telecom group is mostly higher in premarket despite the news.

bullets.title: MSFT: Xbox division facing major layoffs post-June 30; revenue declined ~$500M despite $20B+ investment
bullets.body: Microsoft's Xbox division is planning significant layoffs after fiscal year-end on June 30. Xbox revenue declined nearly $500M annually despite over $20B invested in content and hardware over the past five years, with profit margins at approximately 3%. Additionally, MSFT is restricting internal use of Claude Fable due to data-retention concerns.

bullets.title: NVDA: KKR launches Helix Digital with NVDA as strategic partner; Vistra as preferred power provider
bullets.body: KKR, Kuwait Investment Authority, NVIDIA, and Vistra announced Helix Digital Infrastructure with $10B+ in committed capital for AI-focused data centers. NVDA serves as strategic partner for DSX AI factory-aligned infrastructure deployment. Separately, NVDA has been named lead adopter of advanced process and packaging technologies including first chips on glass substrates, and won OpenAI's Industry AI Acceleration Award. NVDA +1.2% premarket. No confirmed delay to 800VDC architecture—Taiwan supply chain contacts report no notification of pushback.

bullets.title: BABA: Chinese regulators accuse Alibaba, JD, PDD of misleading 618 promotions
bullets.body: Beijing's SAMR cited Alibaba, JD, PDD, ByteDance, and Xiaohongshu for alleged false advertising during the 618 midyear shopping festival. BABA and JD are down in premarket following the regulatory action. Hong Kong-listed Alibaba shares fell nearly 4%.

bullets.title: AXTI: China's control over indium phosphide (InP) flagged as AI datacenter supply risk
bullets.body: Reuters reported that U.S. officials have visited China multiple times to urge resolution of InP export controls without success. AXTI has been identified as a major point of failure in the semiconductor supply chain for photonic chips critical to AI datacenters. U.S. pressure on China to resolve InP export approvals has not yet produced results, driving interest in domestic InP suppliers.

bullets.title: CHWY: FY26 guidance cut ~$200M; JPM cuts PT to $29 but stays OW; MoffettNathanson downgrades to Neutral
bullets.body: Chewy lowered FY26 revenue guidance by ~$200M at midpoint to $13.40-13.55B on softer macro and lower discretionary attach rates. JPM lowered PT from $35 to $29 but kept Overweight, citing 2x+ industry growth, durable margin expansion (FY26 adj. EBITDA 6.6-6.8%), and $500M buyback target. MoffettNathanson downgraded to Neutral. MS also maintains OW at $42 PT, viewing 7x 2027 EBITDA as a compelling entry.

bullets.title: RDDT: Google zero-click searches at 68% pressure Reddit traffic; AXTI/RDDT theses validated
bullets.body: Google zero-click searches reached 68.01% in early 2026 (up from 60.45% in 2024), with AI Overviews reducing click-through rates by nearly 60%. This creates sustained headwinds for RDDT traffic monetization. Separately, one Twitter trader flagged that the RDDT and AXTI investment theses were being validated by Reuters reporting and trade negotiations.

bullets.title: RBRK: Roth and Mizuho reiterate Buy/$90-107 PT; agentic platform and 80% NNARR from high-growth segments
bullets.body: Roth (Buy, $107 PT) and Mizuho (Outperform, $90 PT) both reaffirmed ratings post Rubrik's Analyst Day. Key new disclosures: ~80% of net new ARR from data security apps, cloud, SaaS, and identity; Rubrik Flex licensing enabling larger deals; long-term targets of 20%+ operating margins and 25%+ FCF margins. RBRK growing ARR 25-30% faster than high-growth software median, trading at only 8.2x CY26E EV/ARR.

bullets.title: ACN: Bears see FY27 organic growth at risk from AI-driven margin pressure; clearing event not until Sept
bullets.body: Citi IT Day feedback highlights ACN as a potential casualty of enterprise build-vs-buy shift, with AI reducing in-house tool development costs and accelerating vendor rationalization. Bears cite AI-driven margin risk, high SaaS/BPO/advertising exposure, and no positive near-term catalysts before September guidance. ACN reports June 18 (consensus EPS $3.72, revenue $18.77B).

bullets.title: FSLR: Section 232 tariff decision by end-June could deliver +/-$1.75 EPS upside to 2028+
bullets.body: UBS flags First Solar as a potential beneficiary of the upcoming Section 232 tariff announcement, expected by end of June. Each +/-$0.01/W impact to ASP translates to approximately +/-$1.75 in EPS upside for 2028 and beyond. FSLR is up premarket alongside nuclear and clean energy names.

bullets.title: GNRC: Data center backlog doubles to $700M since mid-February; 2Q26 results potential catalyst
bullets.body: Generac's data center backlog has doubled to $700M since mid-February per UBS. The upcoming 2Q26 results may drive further backlog wins and earnings upside. GNRC is identified as a clean energy/data center infrastructure beneficiary alongside BE and ENPH.

bullets.title: MRVL: $1.1M put sweep signals bearish institutional positioning into Sept expiration
bullets.body: A $1.1M institutional put sweep was detected on MRVL, signaling bearish positioning ahead of the September options expiration. MRVL was also one of the most heavily retail-sold tech names this week (-6.9z selling intensity), alongside ARM (-7.0z) and DELL (-4.0z).
